string.name: whats_new_content
string.translation_description: HTML content listing new features in this release, shown in the What's new dialog and appended to the Help screen. Please do not change the < and > markup.

resources.string:
Curiosity: a new look, and the sky through your camera

Try the new graphics engine (beta)

A more realistic daytime and twilight sky, clearer labels, and a subtle underline on objects that have an info card. It is on by default in this beta. You can switch between Enhanced and Classic any time under Settings → Appearance → Graphics engine. We would love to hear how it works on your phone.

Through-camera mode (beta)

See the sky drawn over your phone\'s live camera image. Turn on Through-camera mode in the Layers sheet, or with the camera button on the layer rail. It is very experimental, and we are still deciding which exposure controls make sense, so tell us what you would want to adjust.

Share the sky

Share what you see from the overflow menu, or with the shutter button in through-camera mode.

Handier layer buttons

The sky colouring and through-camera buttons now sit on the layer rail. The grid and horizon have moved to the Layers sheet.

Recently, in Cassini

  • Satellites: switch on the Satellites layer to find the ISS and Tiangong, and tap one for its next visible passes.
  • Plan your night: info cards show live facts and an Upcoming section for the Moon, planets and meteor showers.
  • Grid and widget: choose how bright the grid lines are, and use the new compact 1x1 Moon phase widget.
  • Better search: find asterisms such as the Big Dipper, and Earth.

And this is just the start...

We have many long asked-for features coming very soon.

About the release name

Curiosity is the NASA rover that has been exploring Gale crater on Mars since landing in 2012, studying whether the planet could once have supported microbial life.

resources.string:
Sky Map comes to iPhone

This is the first iPhone release of Sky Map. It began at Google in 2009 as Google Sky Map, and has been an independent open-source project for well over a decade. Hold your iPhone up and the sky follows your view.

And this is just the start...

More is on the way. Tell us what you would like from the Support screen.

string.name: beta_user_help_text
string.translation_description: Usually-empty HTML content shown to beta testers asking for feedback, appended in the What's new dialog and the Help screen. Please do not change the < and > markup.

resources.string:
Thanks for testing!

Please try the new Graphics engine. It is on by default in this beta (Enhanced under Settings). It draws a more realistic daytime and twilight sky and clearer labels. Tell us if anything looks wrong, especially a black or garbled sky.

Then try through-camera (AR) mode. Turn on Through-camera mode in the Layers sheet to see the sky over the live camera image. It is still very experimental, and we are still deciding which exposure controls make sense, so we would love to hear what you would want to adjust.

You can also share what you see from the overflow menu, or with the shutter in AR mode.

Send feedback from the Support screen.
